figures.text: GPT-6 Astra at medium effort solves 71.9% of mazes on the first attempt, averaged over 48 equally weighted cells. GPT-6.1 Terra (69.7%) is within its interval; Gemini 4 Argon is fourth at 59.1%. Claude Opus 5.5 solves 34.2%, Kimi K3.1 Pro 20.7%, and the two floor models almost nothing. Given four attempts, the leader solves 86%.

Each size level adds rows, columns, rings or rooms and narrows the corridors; L1 is the original v1 medium size. Every model falls at every step: Astra from 93% at L1 to 59% at L4, Claude from 70% to 20%.

title: Bending a maze is harder than enlarging it

figures.text: The four grid families also come warped at every level: the same maze, drawn on a smoothly bent grid, with the same route, endpoints and style. On small mazes the leaders barely notice — Astra loses 9 points at L1. At L4 it falls from 83% to 19%. Claude breaks immediately: it solves 100% of straight L1 grids and 42% of their warped twins.

Every cell holds four mazes. Families are not equally hard, and not hard for the same models: organic mazes (curved, irregular corridors) defeat Claude from L1 and Argon from L2, while island and pipes stay solvable for all three. The leader's hardest cells are the warped L4 grids and the irregular families (organic, radial, cave) at L4.

A per-model logistic regression on maze features. For the two strongest models, corridor width is the largest effect (+1.5 and +1.2 log-odds per SD): narrow corridors make the drawn line clip a wall. For Claude, warping (-1.0) and branching (-1.0) dominate: it loses the route itself. Warping hurts all three, after route length and turns are held fixed.

title: Thinking longer helps on big mazes, for some models

figures.text: The extra-effort settings ran on the 24 L3/L4 cells, compared task by task with the default setting. GPT-6 at xhigh gains 13 points (Astra) and 12 (Sol); Claude at max effort gains 14 while writing about 30× more tokens. Argon is the exception: switching its thinking off costs only 1.3 points, inside the noise. Even at top effort, warped L4 stays below 30% for every model.

Per-attempt list price on L3/L4. GPT-6.1 Terra at medium is the cheapest strong option ($0.011 per attempt for 51%); Astra at xhigh is the most accurate at $0.36. Claude at max effort costs $1.16 per attempt for 32%.

Every failed attempt was classified from its path geometry and, where the model returned one, its reasoning trace; a trace-based label needs the path to agree. 92% of Astra's failures follow the right route and clip a wall: the line runs too close to an edge. Claude cuts across walls (44% of its failures), and in 14% says it will commit to a best-guess path it could not verify. Kimi and Nemotron most often treat the walls as corridors.

Where along the route each failed attempt first touched a wall. Even for the leader, 72% of failures happen in the first half; for Claude and Kimi it is 90% and 91%. Failures are mostly early, local mistakes, not a route that drifts at the end.

Scoring sweeps a 3px pointer disk along the path. Re-scoring every stored submission at other radii changes every score but keeps the order from 1px to 4px. At 5px and above two close pairs swap (Astra and Terra, Sol and Argon) — pairs whose intervals already overlap at 3px.
